             UNANIMOUS STIPULATION AND SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT

        The Signatories to this Unanimous Stipulation and Settlement Agreement (Settlement),

which is dated as of September 15, 2026, are the following:

       Staff of the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Staff);

       Southwestern Electric Power Company (SWEPCO or Company);

       Texas Industrial Energy Consumers (TIEC);

       Office of Public Utility Counsel (OPUC);

       Cities Advocating Reasonable Deregulation (CARD);1and

       Eastman Chemical Company (Eastman).

        The parties to this Settlement shall be referred to individually either as Signatory or by the

acronym assigned above, and collectively as the Signatories.                The Signatories submit this

Settlement to the Commission as representing a just and reasonable disposition of the issues related

to this docket consistent with public interest. The Signatories request approval of this Settlement,

including a new standard form contract for Electric Service – Large Load (ES-LL Contract), filed

Longview, Marshall, Mineola, Mt. Enterprise, Mt. Pleasant, Naples, New London, Pittsburg, Waskom, Wellington,
White Oak, Winnsboro, and Winona.

 contemporaneously with this Settlement as Attachment A, and entry of findings of fact and

conclusions of law consistent with that approval.

         On October 3, 2025, in accordance with Chapter 36 of the Public Utility Regulatory Act

(PURA),2 SWEPCO filed its application with the Commission for authority to amend its tariffs for

retail service to include a new form ES-LL Contract under PURA § 36.001 and 16 Tex. Admin.

Code § 25.241. SWEPCO requested approval of this form contract for the provision of electric

service to new customers with loads greater than 75 megawatts (MW).

         By this Settlement, the Signatories resolve all issues among them related to SWEPCO’s

application in this docket, and agree as follows:

         1.      Revisions to the ES-LL Contract

         The Signatories agree to the following revisions to the proposed ES-LL Contract, which

are incorporated into the version of the Contract included as Attachment A, for which the Parties

are seeking approval by the Commission as part of this Settlement:

         a.      Revise the “Applicability” section to state:

              This form of contract (CONTRACT FOR ELECTRIC SERVICE TEXAS –
              LARGE LOAD) shall apply to any customer whose Contract Capacity (per
              Schedule 1) for computational load, whether new or incremental load, as of the
              date of the execution of this Contract by the Company and the Customer, is
              greater than or equal to 75 MW for any single Computational load facility or
              for multiple Computational loads in aggregate that should be considered a
              single facility for purposes of this Contract. “Computational load” means load
              that primarily consists of power-electronic-based load, specifically
              computational load, such as data centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities.

              SWEPCO may exercise reasonable discretion in determining whether multiple
              Computational loads located in SWEPCO’s Texas service territory should be
              considered a single facility for the purpose of determining the applicability of
              this form of contract based on any reasonable factor, such as whether the loads
              are controlled by the same ultimate entity, whether the loads constitute a single

            points required to serve the requested load.

       The Signatories have agreed to these applicability provisions as a compromise for purposes

of this proceeding, given the specific large loads that have approached SWEPCO, but acknowledge

that the applicability of the ES-LL Contract is an issue that will continue to be evaluated in future

proceedings and that SWEPCO may initiate a filing to address that applicability in the future (with

the parties reserving their rights to take whatever positions they wish regarding any such

application).

       b.       Revise the “Ramp Period” section to state:

            The period beginning with the Beginning Date of Step 1 in Schedule 1 until the
            day prior to the Beginning Date of the last populated Step in Schedule 1, not to
            exceed five years.

       c.       Revise “Initial Contract Term” section to state:

            The period from the day this Contract is executed until eighteen years (18) from
            the inception of the Ramp Period.

       d.       Revise “Minimum Billing Demand (kW)” section to state:

            For purposes of calculating Customer’s bill, during the Billing Period, the
            Billing Demand for each month shall be the greater of the Billing Demand as
            calculated pursuant to the “Determination of Kilowatts of Billing Demand”
            provision of the LLP rate schedule or 90% of the Contract Capacity stated in
            Schedule 1. Outside the Billing Period, the Minimum Billing Demand shall be
            0 MW.

       e.       Revise “Minimum Billing Energy (kWh)” section to state:

            For purposes of calculating Customer’s bill, during the Billing Period, the
            “Kilowatt-hour (kWh) Charge” (¢ per kWh) of the LLP rate schedule shall be
            multiplied times the greater of the actual kWh consumed in the billing period
            or the kWh computed as follows: Contract Capacity stated in Schedule 1 times
            70% times billing hours in the month. Outside the Billing Period, the Minimum
            Billing Energy shall be 0 kWh.

        2.         Analysis, Reporting, Evaluation, and Tracking

       SWEPCO will collaborate with Commission Staff and other parties to determine and

provide analysis, testimony, and supporting workpapers in future base rate case proceedings to

address the following:

       a.         Cost-Shift Review. In SWEPCO’s next base rate case, the Company agrees
                  to include analyses of the costs it has incurred to serve new ES-LL Contract
                  customers, whether those costs have been covered by incremental revenues
                  from the ES-LL Contract customers, and whether any costs to serve ES-LL
                  Contract customers have been shifted to other customers. SWEPCO will
                  provide these analyses, including associated workpapers (in live format)
                  and source documentation, in its application to facilitate discovery and
                  review by the parties and the Commission. The parties reserve their rights
                  to conduct discovery and take any position they wish regarding costs
                  SWEPCO incurs to serve ES-LL Contract customers, and how ES-LL
                  Contract customers should be treated from a ratemaking perspective, in the
                  base rate case and any other appropriate proceeding.

             i.          For purposes of this Cost-Shift Review provision, the term “ES-LL
                         Contract customers” includes new and expanded Computational
                         loads (as set forth in the Applicability section) to whom the
                         parameters of the ES-LL Contract would apply regardless of which
                         of SWEPCO’s jurisdictions the Computational load is located
                         within.

       b.         Post-Base Rate Case Annual Report. Separately, the Company will compile
                  a report to be provided annually to the parties in this proceeding with the
                  same categories of information on an ongoing basis for the period following
                  SWEPCO’s next base rate case, during the interim period prior to
                  SWEPCO’s subsequent base rate case, but after (1) a full twelve-month
                  period following the first customer receiving service under this Contract;
                  and (2) completion of at least Step 1 of Schedule 1. SWEPCO will provide
                  these analyses, including associated workpapers (in live format) and source
                  documentation, in its report to facilitate review by the parties and the
                  Commission. For purposes of this provision, the term “ES-LL Contract
                  customers” includes new loads to whom the parameters of the ES-LL
                  Contract would apply.

       c.         Class Cost of Service (CCOSS) Evaluation. In SWEPCO’s next base rate
                  case, the Company agrees to present two CCOSS and rate designs, one with
                  ES-LL Contract customers as a separate class and the second with ES-LL
                  customers within the LLP-Transmission class. Any party (including
                  SWEPCO) may propose alternative CCOSS and rate design approaches

                with respect to ES-LL Contract customers during any of SWEPCO’s future
               base rate proceedings, as in the usual course. All parties reserve their rights
               to take whatever position they wish on these issues in future proceedings,
               including SWEPCO’s next base rate case.

       d.      Tracking ES-LL Revenues and Costs. SWEPCO agrees to track the non-
               fuel revenues received from the customers under the ES-LL Contract(s), and
               the costs caused by those customers. The Commission will address the
               treatment of those revenues and costs in SWEPCO’s next base-rate
               proceeding. The parties reserve their rights to take whatever positions they
               wish with respect to the proper treatment of those costs and revenues, as
               well as what constitutes a cost caused by an ES-LL Contract customer. For
               purposes of this provision, the term “ES-LL Contract customers” includes
               new and expanded Computational loads (as set forth in the Applicability
               section) to whom the parameters of the ES-LL Contract would apply
               regardless of which of SWEPCO’s jurisdictions the Computational load is
               located within.

       3.      Reservation of Rights

       The Signatories have entered this stipulation as a matter of compromise to facilitate the

implementation of customer safeguards with respect to the specific large Computational loads that

SWEPCO believes are seeking interconnection in the near future. The Signatories acknowledge

that the landscape around large Computational loads, and how those loads should be regulated, is

rapidly changing and that the provisions included in the agreed-to ES-LL Contract will be subject

to further evaluation and potential modification and supplementation in future proceedings,

potentially including rulemaking proceedings. The Signatories reserve their rights to advocate for

different and additional positions regarding the proper regulation of large loads in such future

proceedings, including, without limitation, to which loads the ES-LL Contract should apply and

as to the proper ratemaking treatments that should be adopted with respect to ES-LL Contract

customers.

        4.      CARD’s Rate-Case Expenses

       SWEPCO shall reimburse CARD its reasonable rate-case expenses within 30 days of the

Commission issuing its final order in this proceeding. SWEPCO can seek recovery of those rate-

case expenses in a future proceeding.

       5.      Precedential Nature of Settlement

       Nothing in this Settlement is precedential.

       6.      Obligation to Support this Settlement

       The Signatories support this Settlement and support the Commission’s entry of an order

consistent with this Settlement. The Signatories agree that the Commission should issue the

proposed order, included as Attachment B to this Settlement, which is consistent with the terms of

this Settlement.

       7.      Effect of Settlement in this Proceeding

       a.      There are no third-party beneficiaries of this Settlement, and the Settlement shall

               not be binding on or have any effect on proceedings in other jurisdictions.

               Signatories are not agreeing to any methodology or theory that may support or

               underlie this Settlement.

       b.      This Settlement has been drafted by all the Signatories and is the result of

               negotiation, compromise, settlement, and accommodation. The Signatories agree

               that this Settlement is in the public interest. The terms and conditions in this

               Settlement are intended to work in concert with each other as an integrated whole

               for the purposes of an outcome in this docket that is in the public interest and that

               will result in just and reasonable rates. Thus, the various provisions of this

               Settlement are not severable. None of the provisions of this Settlement shall

              consistent with the terms of this Settlement, each Signatory has the right to

              withdraw from this Settlement, to submit testimony, and to obtain a hearing and

              advocate any position it deems appropriate with respect to any issue in this

      8.      Effect of Settlement on Other Regulatory Proceedings

      a.      This Settlement is binding on each of the Signatories only for the purpose of settling

              the issues as set forth herein in this jurisdiction only and for no other purposes. The

              matters resolved herein are resolved on the basis of a compromise and settlement.

              Except to the extent that this Settlement expressly governs a Signatory’s rights and

              obligations for future periods, this Settlement shall not be binding or precedential

              on a Signatory outside of this proceeding or a proceeding to enforce the terms of

              this Settlement. Each Signatory acknowledges that a Signatory’s support of the

              matters contained in this Settlement may differ from the position taken or testimony

              presented by it in other dockets or other jurisdictions. To the extent that there is a

              difference, a Signatory does not waive its position in any of those other dockets or

              jurisdictions. Because this is a stipulated resolution, no Signatory is under any

              obligation to take the same positions as set out in this Settlement in other dockets

              or jurisdictions, regardless of whether other dockets present the same or a different

              set of circumstances, except as otherwise may be explicitly provided by this

              Settlement. Agreement by the Signatories to any provision in this Settlement will

              not be used against any Signatory in any future proceeding with respect to different

        This Settlement contains the entire understanding and agreement of the Signatories, and it

        Each copy of this Settlement may not bear the signatures of all the Signatories but will be

                                        PROPOSED ORDER

       This Order addresses the application of Southwestern Electric Power Company’s
(SWEPCO or the Company) request for authority to amend its tariffs for retail service to include
a new form Contract for Electric Service – Large Load (ES-LL Contract) for the provision of
electric service to new customers with loads greater than 75 megawatts (75 MW). SWEPCO filed
an unopposed agreement between the parties in this proceeding. The Commission approves the
tariff attached to the agreement as Attachment A, to the extent provided by this Order.

                                   I.       Findings of Fact
